sections.markdown:
## C — Pavement markings and bicycle lanes

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A52
Pavement markings can guide traffic, warn of hazards and impose traffic controls. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A52
Road markings may use yellow, white or a combination of those colors. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A52
A yellow center line separates traffic travelling in opposite directions. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A52
A broken yellow center line permits a left-side pass only when the road ahead is clear; watch for approaching traffic. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A52
With a solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line, passing is permitted from the broken-line side but not the solid-line side. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A52
Double solid yellow center lines prohibit passing in either direction. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A52
The manual permits a left turn across double yellow into or out of an alley, private road or driveway unless signs prohibit it. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A53
The center lane enclosed by solid and broken yellow lines is shared by opposing traffic making left turns. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A53
Enter a shared center turn lane cautiously, use it only for a left turn and never use it to pass. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A53
Signs and pavement arrows help identify a shared left-turn lane. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A53
White lane lines divide traffic travelling in the same direction. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A53
A broken white line may be crossed carefully when changing between same-direction lanes. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A53
Solid white lines identify turn lanes and discourage changing lanes near intersections. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A53
A curved lane arrow accompanied by ONLY requires a turn in that arrow's direction. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A53
A lane showing both a curved arrow and a straight arrow allows either the indicated turn or straight travel. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

Misconceptions: A shared left-turn lane is not a passing lane; a bicycle-lane crossing is different from driving along the lane.
Mnemonics: Color separates directions; line style limits movement; arrows select the path.
Glossary: A center line divides opposing traffic; a lane line divides parallel lanes; a shared lane carries bicycles and motor vehicles.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.

sections.heading: Pavement markings and bicycle lanes
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Pavement markings and bicycle lanes

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A54
A white stop line across an intersection approach marks where a vehicle must stop. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A54
Where a stop line is present, stop at the line rather than beside the sign or signal. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A54
The manual describes an urban stop line as usually about four feet before a crosswalk. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A54
Yield to pedestrians occupying a crosswalk; a crossing can be painted only partly across the road or remain unpainted. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A54
Crosswalks can occur midblock in residential and school areas. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A54
White RxR pavement lettering warns drivers of an approaching railroad crossing. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A54
A yellow line beside the center line can prohibit passing near a railroad crossing. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A54
Rumble strips use sound and vibration to warn an inattentive driver of lane departure or an approaching stop control. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A54
Rumble strips may be on a shoulder, near a two-lane road's center line or in an approach lane before a stop sign or signal. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A54
A two-way center turn lane also serves opposing left-turning vehicles, so use caution and never pass in it. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A54
A designated bicycle lane is reserved for bicycle travel rather than ordinary motor-vehicle travel. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A54
A motorist may cross a bike lane to reach an appropriate travel lane, an on-street parking space or private property. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A54
Before crossing a bike lane, check that the crossing is safe and yield to approaching bicyclists. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A54
For the described turn, wait for a clear bike lane, signal, move into it and then turn. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A55
A shared-lane marking identifies a lane used by both bicycles and motor vehicles and can suggest a preferred bicycle position. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A55
Wait to pass a bicyclist until a safe clearance of at least three feet is available. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]
